Hypothetical

hy-poh-THET-ih-kul — contains 'hypothesis'; a hypothetical situation is just a proposed idea, not yet proven real. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Hypothetical is existing only as an idea or concept; supposed rather than actual.

The debate coach posed a hypothetical case to the students: what if the defendant had a solid alibi the whole time?

Worked Example

Before launching a new spacecraft, engineers spend months imagining every possible failure that could happen -- what if an engine cuts out, what if a valve freezes -- purely on paper, long before any of those things ever actually occur.

Imagining a scenario purely as a possibility, without it necessarily being real, is exactly what hypothetical means. Unlike 'actual,' which describes something real and confirmed, hypothetical describes something only proposed or imagined.

How Hypothetical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

theoretical

theoretical: based on theory rather than actual practice

speculative

speculative: based on guessing rather than known facts

imagined

imagined: existing only in the mind, not in reality

Antonyms

actual

actual: existing in fact; real

factual

factual: based on facts rather than ideas

How Strong Is It? — possible → hypothetical → theoretical

possible vs. hypothetical

possible vs. hypothetical: Possible is a broader, weaker word than hypothetical — something possible simply could happen, while hypothetical specifically describes an idea proposed for the sake of discussion or argument, not a real prediction.

theoretical vs. hypothetical

theoretical vs. hypothetical: Theoretical can feel closely related to hypothetical: hypothetical usually describes a single imagined scenario, while theoretical more often describes a whole framework of ideas not yet tested in practice.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — hypo-

Prefix — hypo-: under, beneath (Greek)

Root — thet

Root — thet: to place, to put (from Greek tithenai -- the same root spelled thes- in thesis)

Suffix — -ical

Suffix — -ical: relating to (Latin/Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Hypo- ('under, beneath') + thet ('to place, to put', from Greek tithenai -- spelled thes- in thesis) + -ical spell hypothetical. Greek hypothesis was literally something 'placed underneath' as a foundation for argument -- something hypothetical is only a proposed foundation for discussion, not yet a confirmed fact.
